answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so influence depends on paths from independently anchored participants, not raw identity count. A Sybil cluster with few attestations crossing its boundary has low conductance; this limits the probability that walk mass enters or remains in the cluster. With capped per-node influence, the bound on that mass limits aggregate voting weight, regardless of whether the cluster is called oasis, garden, or prism.
